name: presentation-abstraction-control
context: Interactive software systems requiring hierarchical organization of autonomous components with clear separation between user interaction, business logic, and inter-agent communication
benefits: Complete decoupling of Presentation and Abstraction through Control mediation
Hierarchical organization for complex semantic concepts
Independent threading enabling fast UI startup before business logic initializes
Scope isolation limiting each agent to contextually relevant data
Support for evolution and extension through well-defined interfaces
Multitasking support for parallel UI and business logic development
tradeoffs: Higher complexity than MVC requiring careful architectural planning
Indirection overhead from Control mediation adding latency
Hierarchy maintenance requiring careful agent relationship design
Event routing complexity as messages traverse hierarchy
Control component criticality as potential bottleneck
Development complexity from complete separation of presentation and abstraction
use_cases: Complex multi-window UIs requiring independent component management
Hierarchical UI components representing semantic concepts
Independent team development of different UI areas
Real-time interactive systems requiring responsive UI
Systems requiring different presentation formats for same data
Applications where UI should start before business logic fully initializes
Multi-user collaborative environments requiring distributed state
avoid_when: Building simple CRUD applications with flat structure
Working with small teams on small-scale projects
Implementing standard web applications with request/response cycles
Strong consistency requirements within a single process
Low latency is critical and indirection overhead is unacceptable
Development team lacks experience with agent-based architectures
component_types: Top-Level-Agent: Application-level coordination, menus, global state, database access
Mid-Level-Agent: Domain area coordination, composes lower-level agents, routes inter-agent communication
Leaf-Agent: Widget-level components (buttons, text fields, sliders, lists) with P-A-C triad
Presentation-Component: Handles user input (mouse, keyboard) and output (visualization, audio)
Abstraction-Component: Represents agent-specific data, business rules, state management
Control-Component: Connects P and A, manages inter-agent communication, message routing
anti_patterns: Distributed monolith (using PAC hierarchy without proper agent boundaries)
Tight coupling between agents (directly accessing other agents' abstractions)
God agents (agents handling too many responsibilities)
Empty hierarchy (using PAC structure without leveraging agent autonomy)
Control bottleneck (centralizing too much logic in top-level control)
Leaking abstractions (allowing Presentation to directly access Abstraction data)
design_principles: Complete Decoupling: Presentation and Abstraction never communicate directly; all communication is mediated by Control
Hierarchical Organization: Agents form a tree-like hierarchy reflecting transitive dependencies between agents
Scope Isolation: Each agent only accesses data that is contextually meaningful within its scope
Autonomous Responsibility: Each agent is responsible for a specific aspect of the application's functionality
Mediated Communication: Inter-agent communication passes through Control components in the hierarchy
Independent Initialization: Presentation can initialize before Abstraction, enabling fast UI startup
Encapsulated Facets: Each agent's three facets (P, A, C) are tightly coupled internally but loosely coupled externally
best_practices: Agent Granularity: Balance between small focused agents (flexibility) and larger efficient agents (overhead)
Hierarchy Depth: Limit hierarchy depth to manage complexity; deep hierarchies increase message routing overhead
Control Simplicity: Keep Control components focused on routing; delegate business logic to Abstraction
Message Design: Use typed messages with clear contracts for inter-agent communication
State Management: If state is required, manage it in Abstraction components; keep Presentation stateless
Error Handling: Implement error propagation through hierarchy with appropriate fallback handling
Monitoring: Add metrics at each agent level for system observability
